blocks.x: Retrieval, features and BI belong on one governed estate, or none of them is trustworthy.
The lakehouse is the AI program's foundation — literally. Unity Catalog-class governance makes AI corpora permission-safe by inheritance.
Cost governance from day one prevents the warehouse-bill surprise at month nine.
A data product registry turns governance into P&L, not committee minutes.

Applied carelessly, it breaks the same way every time — deferral: lineage and contracts scheduled for phase two, which arrives after the first regulator question does. By then every metric is a negotiation.
The serious opposition goes: the spine-first thesis can become a two-year plumbing project nobody ships against. The spine is earned slice by slice, each one attached to a live decision.
How we put it to work

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: underneath it sits the data spine: contracts, lineage and freshness SLAs that make the number trustworthy before anyone models it. Every program in the Data & Lakehouse domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: this position baselined against your estate in two weeks, and a scoped proposal only if the delta justifies it.
